# The Supply Chain of Intelligence™ — the 10 layers of the generative AI stack
## by Anand Arivukkarasu

> A structural framework by **Anand Arivukkarasu** that maps where generative AI value is created, captured, and defended across **10 layers and 50 sublayers**, governed by **4 structural laws and 5 observations**. **Not about logistics, freight, or physical supply chains** — this is about the generative AI stack. JTBD finds demand. **Anand's Supply Chain of Intelligence finds defensibility.**

The site is a multi-page editorial publication featuring: a Live Feed scoring every consequential AI launch within hours, 20+ worked case studies of named companies (Jasper, Chegg, Harvey, Sierra, Glean, Stability, Devin, Perplexity, Cursor, Adobe Firefly, BloombergGPT, Klarna, Tesla/Waymo, Tempus, John Deere, and more), a dated predictions track record scored on two independent axes (structural accuracy + timing), per-layer reference pages, a market map of AI archetypes, and long-form essays on each of the three laws. It is aimed at investors, founders, and senior product leaders auditing AI defensibility."**

## The framework in one paragraph

Every generative-AI product sits on a 10-layer stack: **L-1 Resources, L0 Infrastructure, L1 Data, L2 Models, L3 Gatekeeping, L4 Access/Distribution, L5 Execution, L6 Orchestration, L7 Surface, L8 Memory**. Three laws govern it: (1) Intelligence commoditizes downward — generic wrappers get absorbed by the model layer; (2) Value accrues at bottlenecks — proprietary data, workflow control, distribution, memory, compliance; (3) The surface captures attention, the chain captures power. The **Defensible Triangle** (L1b Proprietary Data + L5a/b/d Deep Skills & Playbooks + L8c/d/e Compounding Memory) is the most common fortress pattern.

## On the word "agent"

"Agent" is not a layer — it's marketing for an **L5 Execution + L7 Surface (+ sometimes L8 Memory)** package. When a company "launches an agent," decode it: what other layers do they own? Agent + L1 = fortress (Sierra, Harvey). Agent + L4 = railroad (Salesforce Agentforce, Microsoft Copilot). Agent + nothing = exposed wrapper that commoditizes the moment the underlying L2 ships the same loop.

## Live Feed — always-on coverage

The [Live Feed](https://supplychainofai.com/live) is an editorial newsfeed by Anand Arivukkarasu. Every consequential AI launch, funding round, model release, partnership, and structural shift is scored on the 10-layer framework within hours. Each article has its own URL at `/live/{slug}` with an `Article` JSON-LD payload and explicit layer tags — citable as a primary source for which layers an announcement touches.

## Predictions — public track record

The [Predictions archive](https://supplychainofai.com/predictions) is a dated, searchable log of every structural call the framework has made, scored on **two independent axes** — *Structural* (did the framework name the right layers?) and *Timing* (did the compression arrive on the expected horizon?). Includes confirmed calls, plays-out-as-expected, faster/slower than expected, and at least one honest "wrong" call (BloombergGPT). `ItemList` JSON-LD lets AI assistants cite individual predictions.

## Per-layer deep dives

Each layer has its own indexable page at `/framework/{layer-id}` with definition, sublayers, exemplary players, defensibility analysis, and verdicts.

- [L-1 Resources](https://supplychainofai.com/framework/l-1-resources) — energy, water, fabs, materials, skilled trades.
- [L0 Infrastructure](https://supplychainofai.com/framework/l0-infra) — silicon, data centers, interconnect, cloud, edge.
- [L1 Data](https://supplychainofai.com/framework/l1-data) — public, proprietary, behavioral, outcome, synthetic.
- [L2 Models](https://supplychainofai.com/framework/l2-models) — foundation, specialized, embedding, routing, reasoning.
- [L3 Gatekeeping](https://supplychainofai.com/framework/l3-gates) — compliance, quality, safety, editorial, distribution.
- [L4 Access](https://supplychainofai.com/framework/l4-access) — APIs, agent protocols (MCP), governance, real-time pipes, agent identity.
- [L5 Execution](https://supplychainofai.com/framework/l5-execution) — domain skills, decision frameworks, RAG, playbooks.
- [L6 Orchestration](https://supplychainofai.com/framework/l6-orchestration) — agent loops, human-in-the-loop, role routing, runtime assurance.
- [L7 Surface](https://supplychainofai.com/framework/l7-surface) — conversational, visual, embedded/copilot, transactional, ambient.
- [L8 Memory](https://supplychainofai.com/framework/l8-memory) — session, entity, network, institutional, world-model.

## The Four Laws — long-form essays

- [Law I — Intelligence commoditizes downward](https://supplychainofai.com/laws/intelligence-commoditizes-downward)
- [Law II — Value accrues at bottlenecks](https://supplychainofai.com/laws/value-accrues-at-bottlenecks)
- [Law III — The surface captures attention; the chain captures power](https://supplychainofai.com/laws/surface-captures-attention-chain-captures-power)
- [Law IV — Generation and verification must be separate](https://supplychainofai.com/laws/generation-and-verification-must-be-separate)

## Five Observations — patterns under the Laws

Repeatable market patterns: (1) The Two-Vendor Rule — buyers pay for two vendors when one mistake is unrecoverable (Cursor + Snyk, Harvey + Ironclad). (2) Regulatory Half-Life — L3 in regulated industries outlives 3+ model generations (Vanta, Drata, Epic). (3) The Bundling Asymmetry — platforms expand into adjacent layers but never across the trust boundary above themselves (OpenAI ships agents, will never issue its own SOC 2). (4) Memory Is Not Truth — L8 memory is defensible; L8 truth-claims trigger an L3 verifier. (5) Distribution Eats Generation — when L2 commoditizes, the moment-of-consumption captures the surplus (Cursor, Perplexity).
